Purchasing Supplies on Sponsored Awards

From the ORA eTraining module "Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects" (lesson 10 of 15).
Purchasing Supplies on Sponsored Projects
Supplies ( 2CFR200.453 ) are commonly needed to support the day-to-day work of a sponsored project. Supply, and other procurement, orders must be delivered to MSU main campus or an MSU-owned satellite location (such as MSU PEARL). When supplies are purchased with sponsored funds, the purchase must follow sponsor requirements, Uniform Guidance, and MSU Procurement rules. The key question is not only “Can we buy this?” but also “Can we clearly document why this purchase benefits the sponsored project?”
Complete the content above before moving on.
What is a Micro-Purchase?
A micro-purchase is a low-dollar procurement of supplies or services that falls at or below Morgan State University’s micro-purchase threshold of $5,000 per transaction . The current federal micro-purchase threshold under FAR 2.101 is generally $15,000 , and 2 CFR 200.320 allows recipients to use lower institutional thresholds. Morgan applies a more restrictive institutional limit of $5,000 , so MSU users must follow the lower threshold. 2 CFR 200.320 states that micro-purchases may be awarded without soliciting competitive price or rate quotations if the recipient considers the price reasonable and maintains documentation supporting that conclusion.

Price Reasonableness in Procurements
Even when quotes are not required, MSU personnel must still be responsible stewards of University and sponsored funds. The price must be fair and reasonable. The documentation does not need to be complicated, but it should be clear enough for a reviewer, auditor, or sponsor to understand why the price was considered reasonable. Ways to support price reasonableness may include: Comparing vendors to identify a fair or lower price Reviewing prior purchases of the same or similar item Using an established or preferred vendor Considering less expensive alternatives if they would still meet the project need Confirming that the item is not unusually priced compared to market expectations

Additional Purchasing Guidelines
Required Documentation
Whether the purchase is made by p-card or requisition, your files should include enough documentation to support the business purpose, project benefit, and allowability of the expense. At minimum, include: Receipt or invoice Business purpose (allocability to the project's NOA) Confirmation that the cost occurred during the project period of performance Confirmation that the cost is allocable to the award being charged Please refer to the " Processing Invoices for Payment " lesson in this module for key invoice components.
Preferred Vendors
Before purchasing supplies, check whether the item is available through: Existing State contracts MSU preferred vendors MBE, SBE, VSBE, or other certified vendor options, when applicable Using established contracts or preferred vendors can improve compliance, reduce processing time, and support institutional procurement goals.
Sponsor-Specific restrictions
Always check sponsor-specific guidance before purchasing supplies. Examples include: NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIH GPS) NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (NSF PAPPG) Award terms and conditions Sponsor prior approval requirements Restrictions in the approved budget or Notice of Award Some sponsors may restrict certain types of purchases, require prior approval, or expect additional documentation for items that appear unusual, high-risk, or not clearly tied to the project scope.
Technology Procurements
Technology-related purchases may require additional review before purchase. This may include: Computers, tablets, software, cloud-based tools, data storage, etc. Before purchasing technology, review Morgan's IT minimum hardware requirements to ensure they meet the product specifications necessary to link with Morgan's domain and IT support. Preferred vendors should be used when possible, especially for technology purchases, to help ensure compatibility with MSU systems and institutional standards.
Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: A PI has $4,800 remaining on a federal award that ends next month. The PI wants to purchase general office supplies for the department because the funds are available. Is this allowable?
  - Yes  [incorrect]
  - No  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  If correct: Great job! The purchase does not appear allocable to the sponsored project and may not benefit the award during the period of performance.
  If incorrect: Try again. Remember our guidelines on end-of-period purchasing and general office supply procurements.
